targets.description: The author disputes the claim that placebo treatments activate a powerful general healing mechanism.
The article distinguishes subjective patient-reported outcomes from objective outcomes such as survival and tumor shrinkage.
Named reviews and reanalyses attribute apparent placebo benefits to small subjective effects, biased reporting, natural history, regression to the mean, and trial artifacts.
Open-label placebo, veterinary, and health-governor examples are assessed separately rather than blended into one body of evidence.
Systematic reviews find little general clinically important placebo effect
Classic placebo estimates are weakened by reanalysis of study design and natural-history effects
Open-label placebo trials retain expectancy-producing scripts and other methodological problems
Veterinary placebo findings demonstrate observer or caregiver reporting effects rather than confirmed animal improvement
The proposed biological health governor is presented as speculative rather than established

targets.excerpt: Placebo interventions for all clinical conditions
The Powerful Placebo Effect: Fact or Fiction?
open-label placebo trial for chronic low back pain
owners reported improvement roughly 57% of the time

prohibitedInterpretations: Findings from different reviews, trials, diseases, species, or outcome types are merged into one study.
Small changes in subjective pain or nausea are converted into objective biological healing.
Open-label placebo trials are described as entirely free of expectancy cues or deception concerns.
Owner-reported improvement in dogs is treated as medically confirmed improvement in the animals.
The health-governor hypothesis is presented as an empirically established mechanism.
The author claims that contextual care and patient perception can never affect reported symptoms.
reviewNotes: Keep the identity, date, population, endpoint, and limitation of each named work attached to that work.
The article quotes claims it criticizes; preserve the distinction between Phil Starks, cited researchers, study participants, and David Gorski's conclusions.
